targets.canonical_science: Chlorophyll is a photosynthetic pigment embedded in thylakoid membranes that absorbs light used to excite electrons in photosystems.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? A _____ is a discrete quantum of electromagnetic radiation; _____ energy is inversely related to wavelength.
targets.hint: one discrete light pulse compared across short- and long-wavelength paths
targets.canonical_science: A photon is a discrete quantum of electromagnetic radiation; photon energy is inversely related to wavelength.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? _____ is the distance between corresponding points of successive waves; shorter-_____ photons carry more energy than longer-_____ photons.
targets.hint: the crest-to-crest ruler showing shorter versus longer _____
targets.canonical_science: Wavelength is the distance between corresponding points of successive waves; shorter-wavelength photons carry more energy than longer-wavelength photons.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? _____ is the primary reaction-center pigment in oxygenic photosynthesis.
targets.hint: the _____ panel connected to the reaction-center role
targets.canonical_science: Chlorophyll a is the primary reaction-center pigment in oxygenic photosynthesis.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? _____ is an accessory _____ that broadens the wavelengths usable for photosynthesis in plants and green algae.
targets.hint: the _____ panel broadening usable wavelengths
targets.canonical_science: Chlorophyll b is an accessory chlorophyll that broadens the wavelengths usable for photosynthesis in plants and green algae.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? _____ are accessory pigments that broaden light absorption and can dissipate excess light energy, helping protect the photosynthetic apparatus.
targets.hint: the _____ panel broadening absorption and dissipating excess excitation
targets.canonical_science: Carotenoids are accessory pigments that broaden light absorption and can dissipate excess light energy, helping protect the photosynthetic apparatus.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? A _____ is a thylakoid-membrane complex containing a reaction center and surrounding light-harvesting pigments and proteins.
targets.hint: the complete antenna-plus-reaction-center complex embedded in thylakoid membrane
targets.canonical_science: A photosystem is a thylakoid-membrane complex containing a reaction center and surrounding light-harvesting pigments and proteins.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? A photosystem _____ contains a special chlorophyll pair and primary electron acceptor where excitation leads to electron transfer.
targets.hint: the central special chlorophyll pair beside a primary electron acceptor
targets.canonical_science: A photosystem reaction center contains a special chlorophyll pair and primary electron acceptor where excitation leads to electron transfer.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? _____es contain pigment molecules bound to proteins and transfer excitation energy toward the reaction center.
targets.hint: the surrounding pigment-protein antenna transferring excitation toward the center
targets.canonical_science: Light-harvesting complexes contain pigment molecules bound to proteins and transfer excitation energy toward the reaction center.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? _____ absorbs light, transfers an excited electron to an acceptor, and receives replacement electrons from water oxidation.
targets.hint: the _____ reaction center transferring an excited electron to an acceptor
targets.canonical_science: Photosystem II absorbs light, transfers an excited electron to an acceptor, and receives replacement electrons from water oxidation.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? _____ re-excites electrons arriving from the thylakoid electron transport chain and supports reduction of NADP+ to NADPH.
targets.hint: the _____ reaction center re-exciting the incoming electron with a second light input
targets.canonical_science: Photosystem I re-excites electrons arriving from the thylakoid electron transport chain and supports reduction of NADP+ to NADPH.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? The _____ is a _____ carbon-fixation pathway in the chloroplast stroma that uses ATP and NADPH to incorporate CO2 into carbohydrate.
targets.hint: the circular stroma pathway using ATP and NADPH while carbon enters and the acceptor is regenerated
targets.canonical_science: The Calvin cycle is a cyclic carbon-fixation pathway in the chloroplast stroma that uses ATP and NADPH to incorporate CO2 into carbohydrate.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? _____ is incorporation of inorganic CO2 into an organic molecule; in the Calvin cycle CO2 is added to a _____ acceptor.
targets.hint: the amber _____ tracer leaving inorganic CO₂ and becoming part of an organic _____ framework at the central bench
targets.canonical_science: Carbon fixation is incorporation of inorganic CO2 into an organic molecule; in the Calvin cycle CO2 is added to a carbon acceptor.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? _____ is the enzyme that catalyzes the initial CO2-fixation reaction of the Calvin cycle and can also react with O2.
targets.hint: the large central _____ enzyme docking CO₂ and RuBP without being consumed as either substrate
targets.canonical_science: Rubisco is the enzyme that catalyzes the initial CO2-fixation reaction of the Calvin cycle and can also react with O2.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? Ribulose bisphosphate (_____) is the CO2-acceptor molecule regenerated in the Calvin cycle.
targets.hint: the five-carbon _____ acceptor waiting on the right rack and returning after regeneration
targets.canonical_science: Ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP) is the CO2-acceptor molecule regenerated in the Calvin cycle.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate (_____) is a three-carbon sugar produced by the Calvin cycle and can be used to synthesize glucose and other organic molecules.
targets.hint: the three-carbon _____ molecule leaving through the left output gate toward organic-molecule synthesis
targets.canonical_science: Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate (G3P) is a three-carbon sugar produced by the Calvin cycle and can be used to synthesize glucose and other organic molecules.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? _____ occurs when rubisco reacts with O2 instead of CO2, consuming energy and lowering net carbon fixation; it is favored when internal CO2 is low relative to O2.
targets.hint: rubisco at a branch where O₂ sends the reaction into a right-side detour and the net-carbon-gain gauge falls
targets.canonical_science: Photorespiration occurs when rubisco reacts with O2 instead of CO2, consuming energy and lowering net carbon fixation; it is favored when internal CO2 is low relative to O2.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? C4 plants initially fix CO2 into four-carbon compounds in mesophyll cells and deliver concentrated CO2 to bundle-sheath cells, reducing photorespiration through spatial separation.
targets.hint: the left C4 leaf model separating initial fixation in mesophyll from Calvin-cycle processing in bundle-sheath cells
targets.canonical_science: C4 plants initially fix CO2 into four-carbon compounds in mesophyll cells and deliver concentrated CO2 to bundle-sheath cells, reducing photorespiration through spatial separation.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? _____ plants open stomata mainly at night, store fixed carbon in organic acids, and release CO2 during the day for the Calvin cycle, reducing water loss through temporal separation.
targets.hint: the right _____ leaf model opening stomata at night, storing carbon in organic acids, and releasing CO₂ during the day
targets.canonical_science: CAM plants open stomata mainly at night, store fixed carbon in organic acids, and release CO2 during the day for the Calvin cycle, reducing water loss through temporal separation.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? _____+ accepts electrons and a proton to become _____; _____ carries high-energy electrons to other reactions including the respiratory electron transport chain.
targets.hint: the _____⁺ carrier closing around transferred electrons and becoming _____
targets.canonical_science: NAD+ accepts electrons and a proton to become NADH; NADH carries high-energy electrons to other reactions including the respiratory electron transport chain.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? _____ accepts electrons and protons during the citric acid cycle to become FADH2, which can deliver electrons to the respiratory electron transport chain.
targets.hint: the _____ carrier becoming FADH₂ when loaded with electrons and protons during the citric acid cycle
targets.canonical_science: FAD accepts electrons and protons during the citric acid cycle to become FADH2, which can deliver electrons to the respiratory electron transport chain.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? _____ forms ATP by direct enzymatic transfer of a _____ group from an organic _____ to ADP.
targets.hint: a _____ transferred directly from an organic _____ intermediate to ADP without ATP synthase
targets.canonical_science: Substrate-level phosphorylation forms ATP by direct enzymatic transfer of a phosphate group from an organic substrate to ADP.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? During standard aerobic eukaryotic respiration, _____ is transported into mitochondria and oxidized to an acetyl group carried by coenzyme A, producing CO2 and NADH.
targets.hint: three-carbon _____ entering the airlock, losing CO₂, reducing NAD⁺, and leaving as a two-carbon acetyl group
targets.canonical_science: During standard aerobic eukaryotic respiration, pyruvate is transported into mitochondria and oxidized to an acetyl group carried by coenzyme A, producing CO2 and NADH.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? _____ coenzyme A (_____) carries a two-carbon _____ group into the citric acid cycle.
targets.hint: the two-carbon _____ group attached to a coenzyme A handle and entering the cycle
targets.canonical_science: Acetyl coenzyme A (acetyl-CoA) carries a two-carbon acetyl group into the citric acid cycle.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? The _____, also called the Krebs _____, oxidizes acetyl groups in the mitochondrial matrix and transfers energy to ATP, NADH, and FADH2 while releasing CO2.
targets.hint: the circular matrix pathway oxidizing acetyl-derived carbon and regenerating its acceptor
targets.canonical_science: The citric acid cycle, also called the Krebs cycle, oxidizes acetyl groups in the mitochondrial matrix and transfers energy to ATP, NADH, and FADH2 while releasing CO2.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? _____ _____ includes electron transport that establishes a proton gradient and chemiosmosis through ATP synthase.
targets.hint: the two linked _____ of _____ _____, respiratory electron transport and ATP-synthase chemiosmosis
targets.canonical_science: Oxidative phosphorylation includes electron transport that establishes a proton gradient and chemiosmosis through ATP synthase.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? The _____ ETC is a series of inner-membrane _____ carriers that undergo redox reactions and transfer _____ toward a terminal acceptor.
targets.hint: the series of inner-membrane redox carriers passing _____ stepwise toward a terminal acceptor
targets.canonical_science: The respiratory ETC is a series of inner-membrane electron carriers that undergo redox reactions and transfer electrons toward a terminal acceptor.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? _____ is the use of energy stored in an electrochemical proton gradient as protons move through a membrane-associated process such as ATP synthase.
targets.hint: H⁺ moving down an electrochemical gradient through the membrane-associated ATP synthase process
targets.canonical_science: Chemiosmosis is the use of energy stored in an electrochemical proton gradient as protons move through a membrane-associated process such as ATP synthase.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? _____ is a membrane enzyme complex that uses proton-motive force to catalyze formation of _____ from ADP and inorganic phosphate.
targets.hint: the membrane-spanning _____ complex using proton-motive force to form _____ from ADP and inorganic phosphate
targets.canonical_science: ATP synthase is a membrane enzyme complex that uses proton-motive force to catalyze formation of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? _____ uses an electron transport chain with a terminal electron acceptor other than oxygen.
targets.hint: the upper-right ETC route ending at a non-oxygen terminal acceptor rather than the oxygen basin
targets.canonical_science: Anaerobic respiration uses an electron transport chain with a terminal electron acceptor other than oxygen.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? _____ regenerates NAD+ without an electron transport chain so glycolysis can continue when oxidative NADH reoxidation cannot meet demand.
targets.hint: the cytosolic redox gate where NADH transfers reducing power to an organic molecule without an ETC
targets.canonical_science: Fermentation regenerates NAD+ without an electron transport chain so glycolysis can continue when oxidative NADH reoxidation cannot meet demand.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? _____ converts pyruvate to ethanol and CO2 while oxidizing NADH to regenerate NAD+.
targets.hint: the three-station _____ route: pyruvate loses CO₂, acetaldehyde forms, then NADH reduction produces ethanol and NAD⁺
targets.canonical_science: Alcohol fermentation converts pyruvate to ethanol and CO2 while oxidizing NADH to regenerate NAD+.

targets.prompt: Which exact Unit 3 name matches this scientific description? In _____-producing fermentation, pyruvate is reduced by NADH to _____, regenerating NAD+.
targets.hint: the direct three-carbon pyruvate-to-_____ reaction returning NADH to NAD⁺ without a CO₂ vent
targets.canonical_science: In lactate-producing fermentation, pyruvate is reduced by NADH to lactate, regenerating NAD+.
